info.name: XeltaCraft — Gemini World Build
info.description:
Calls the real Google Gemini generateContent endpoint directly, with the exact same system prompt, generationConfig, and responseSchema as ai.xelta.craft.api.GeminiArchitectClient.java. No caching exists anywhere in that Java path (verified by code search + live logs showing 15-60s round trips) — this collection hits Gemini live every time, same as the mod.

Set collection variables: api_key (required), prompt, block_size. Optionally set image_base64 (+ image_mime) to attach a reference image — see the request's pre-request script comment for how to base64-encode a file on Windows.

Check the response's 'Time' badge in Postman after sending — a live Gemini call takes ~15-60s (longer with an image attached); anything near-instant would be the only real sign of caching, and nothing in this collection or the mod's code path caches.

exec: // Exact copy of GeminiArchitectClient.SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE — a JS template literal so the
// prompt's own literal '{' '}' JSON-schema examples never collide with any substitution syntax.
// Keep this in sync by hand if the Java prompt changes.
const SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE = `You are a Master Architect for the X-DAVE AI-Native Voxel Generation Engine. You design highly aesthetic, structurally sound, and beautiful buildings.
Your task is to analyze a natural language prompt and return a Semantic Object Graph.
- The structure footprint must fit within {block_size} x {block_size} blocks.

- The overall scene should suggest a style. If the user's inventory contains blocks, you MUST set the 'style' and 'material' fields to exact block IDs from their inventory (e.g., 'minecraft:cobblestone') to ensure you use their available resources.
- The 'scale' of the scene should be determined (e.g. small, medium, large).
- IMPORTANT: Use pre-designed architectural macros whenever possible by setting 'type' to exactly 'gothic_arch' or 'watchtower_roof'.
Output ONLY a valid JSON object matching this schema:

Populate AT MOST ONE of 'house', 'tower', 'castle' — whichever matches the request — and leave the other two null. For every other structure type (walls, roofs, furniture, decorations, anything else) leave all three null.
If the request describes a house/building/cottage, populate 'house' with real per-wall detail:

Include exactly one wall entry per side (NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST) that has an opening — omit a side entirely if it has no door/window. Exactly one wall in the whole house should have a DOOR opening (the entrance); any wall may have WINDOW openings. 'offset' must be strictly between 0 and that wall's length (width for NORTH/SOUTH, depth for EAST/WEST) minus 1.

Choose 'roofType' to match the request: 'GABLE' for a classic two-sided pitched roof (cottages, cabins, farmhouses — this is the default when the request doesn't imply anything else), 'HIP' for a roof that slopes down on all four sides instead of having flat gable ends (bungalows, symmetric or villa-style homes), or 'FLAT' for a flat modern roof, optionally with a low parapet ledge (modern, urban, or minimalist builds).

Only populate 'annex' when the request implies an attached porch, wing, sunroom, garage, or otherwise asymmetric/L-shaped footprint (e.g. "a cottage with a small porch", "an L-shaped farmhouse") — leave it null for a plain single-rectangle house. When populated:

The annex is a second room positioned relative to the main house's (0,0) corner — pick offsetX/offsetZ so it sits FLUSH against one side of the main house rather than floating away from it (e.g. offsetX = the main house's width to attach an annex to its east side, offsetZ = 0 to align its north edge with the main house's north edge). Keep the annex smaller than the main house.
If the request describes a tower/watchtower/spire, populate 'tower':
If the request describes a castle/keep/fortress, populate 'castle':
A castle always gets a real cylindrical tower at each of its 4 corners automatically — do not describe the towers as separate objects.
Do NOT output blocks or coordinates. Output ONLY valid JSON. Do NOT include markdown code blocks, explanations, or any other text.`;
properties: { type: typeSchema('STRING'), position: typeSchema('STRING'), scale: typeSchema('NUMBER'), material: typeSchema('STRING') },
properties: { objects: { type: 'ARRAY', items: sceneObjectSchema }, style: typeSchema('STRING'), scale: typeSchema('STRING') },
const openingSchema = { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { type: typeSchema('STRING'), offset: typeSchema('INTEGER') }, required: ['type', 'offset'] };
items: { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { facing: typeSchema('STRING'), openings: { type: 'ARRAY', items: openingSchema } }, required: ['facing', 'openings'] }
properties: { width: typeSchema('INTEGER'), depth: typeSchema('INTEGER'), wallHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER'), offsetX: typeSchema('INTEGER'), offsetZ: typeSchema('INTEGER'), walls: wallsArraySchema }

properties: { width: typeSchema('INTEGER'), depth: typeSchema('INTEGER'), wallHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER'), pitchHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER'), roofType: typeSchema('STRING'), walls: wallsArraySchema, annex: annexSchema }
properties: { radius: typeSchema('INTEGER'), height: typeSchema('INTEGER'), crenellated: typeSchema('BOOLEAN'), roofHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER') }

properties: { width: typeSchema('INTEGER'), depth: typeSchema('INTEGER'), wallHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER'), towerRadius: typeSchema('INTEGER'), towerHeight: typeSchema('INTEGER'), gateWall: typeSchema('STRING'), gateOffset: typeSchema('INTEGER') }
properties: { scene: sceneSchema, house: houseSchema, tower: towerSchema, castle: castleSchema },
const parts = [{ text: 'Generate the Semantic Object Graph now. Output ONLY the JSON object.' }];
parts.push({ inline_data: { mime_type: pm.collectionVariables.get('image_mime') || 'image/png', data: imageBase64.trim() } });

request.description:
To attach a reference image: base64-encode a file and set it as the 'image_base64' collection variable (leave empty for a text-only call, same as most of the mod's builds).

Windows (PowerShell): [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('C:\path\to\image.jpg')) | Set-Clipboard
Windows (cmd, chunked): certutil -encode image.jpg image.b64  (then strip the ---BEGIN/END--- lines)
Or just run: python test_gemini_api.py "..." --image path\to\image.jpg  which does this for you and prints full diagnostics without any Postman setup.
